name: Principles of Surgical Oncology, Resection Margins, and Soft Tissue Sarcomas

reference.source: Sabiston Textbook of Surgery 22nd ed / Society of Surgical Oncology Guidelines
clinicalPearls: Resection margin status is defined as R0 (microscopically negative), R1 (microscopically positive), and R2 (macroscopically positive gross tumor)
En bloc anatomical tumor resection adheres to the no-touch isolation technique to prevent intraoperative neoplastic cell dissemination
Soft tissue sarcomas require core needle biopsy oriented along the planned longitudinal axis of the definitive surgical excision
Standard extremity sarcoma excision mandates wide local excision with 1 to 2 cm margins including an intact anatomical fascial barrier
Retroperitoneal sarcomas are managed with complete compartmental en bloc resection of the tumor along with contiguous adherent organs
reference.pathophysiology: Malignant neoplasms progress through uncontrolled clonal proliferation, local tissue invasion, angiogenesis, and lymphatic or hematogenous dissemination. Soft tissue sarcomas arise from mesenchymal lineages (adipose, muscle, nerve sheath, fibrous tissue) and characteristically form a pseudocapsule of compressed neoplastic cells and reactive fibrous stroma. Simple enucleation through this pseudocapsule inevitably leaves microscopic disease (R1/R2) resulting in high local recurrence. Multimodal therapy combining preoperative radiotherapy and wide margin surgery optimizes local control and limb salvage.
additionalDifferentials: Deep intramuscular lipoma versus well-differentiated liposarcoma
Retroperitoneal sarcoma versus metastatic lymphadenopathy or gastrointestinal stromal tumor
Desmoid tumor (aggressive fibromatosis) versus low-grade fibrosarcoma
Benign schwannoma versus malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor (MPNST)
additionalInvestigations: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with contrast of the extremity for precise soft-tissue tumor planes and neurovascular bundle relation
Multislice contrast-enhanced CT of chest, abdomen, and pelvis to detect pulmonary metastases in sarcoma staging
Image-guided core needle biopsy (14-gauge) with histological grading (FNCLCC grading system)
Molecular cytogenetic testing (e.g., MDM2 amplification for liposarcoma, SS18-SSX translocation for synovial sarcoma)
